reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table matches what Alpha reported (order 113 for 7379 cents and order 115 for 6651 cents), so I'll check the refunds first.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly (order 113 for 7379 cents and order 115 for 6651 cents), so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll call list_orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme, before recording any payouts.
Acme's net balance came back as 22142 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance before recording any payouts.
Acme's and birch's balances are already in hand, and I have the refunds check. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance before recording any payouts.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and I have net balances for all three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll record the first payout, for acme at 22142 cents.
Acme's payout of 22142 cents recorded successfully. The refunds matched Alpha's report, so I'll record birch's payout of 49030 cents next, then cobalt's.
Birch's payout of 49030 cents is recorded. Cobalt's net balance is 33952 cents, so I'll record that payout now to finish the batch.
All three payouts recorded successfully, and each matches its order total minus refunds (acme 29521 - 7379 = 22142, birch 49030, cobalt 40603 - 6651 = 33952). The batch is complete.
